brief: I'm Gary Pruitt, treasurer of the Mount Pleasant Volunteer Fire Company in Mount Pleasant, Pennsylvania. I need a flyer for our Pancake Breakfast, 1275 x 1650 portrait, to print on letter paper for the post office, the diner and the school, and to post on our Facebook page. Facts: Sunday, March 15, 7 a.m. to 11 a.m., at the firehouse on Church Street (Station 12); all you can eat pancakes, sausage, eggs and coffee; $9 adults, $5 kids 6 to 12, kids under 6 eat free; family max $28; proceeds buy new turnout gear, we need 6 sets at $3,400 each; Engine 12 will be out front and kids can sit in the cab. Takeout boxes available. Tone: friendly, small-town, a little proud. No photos available. Do not invent a phone number, a website or a sponsor. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Priya Natarajan, owner of Little Oven Bakery on Division Street in Grand Rapids, Michigan. We are launching a new loaf and I need an Instagram square, 1080 x 1080, to announce it. Facts: it's a rosemary and sea salt sourdough called 'The Hearth Loaf'; 36-hour ferment; $9 a loaf; baked Fridays and Saturdays only, 60 loaves each day, out of the oven at 8 a.m.; first bake is Friday, April 4; you can reserve a loaf in the shop until Thursday at noon. Tone: quiet, confident, handmade, not cutesy. No photos available. Text should be short enough to read on a phone while scrolling. Do not invent a website, a discount or a phone number. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Walt Hendrickson, volunteer chair of the Cedar Hollow Bluegrass Festival in Galax, Virginia. I need the lineup poster, 1200 x 1800 portrait, to print at 24 x 36 and post online. Facts: three days, Friday, June 12 through Sunday, June 14, at Cedar Hollow Park; headliners are the Ridgeline Ramblers (Friday), Misty Orchard (Saturday) and the Hartsell Family Singers (Sunday); also playing: Dry Creek Boys, Annalise Cobb and Company, Tuckahoe Strings, Little Rhody Mae and the Pine Mountain Pickers; gates open at noon daily; $25 a day, $60 for the weekend, kids 12 and under free; camping $15 a night; bring a lawn chair, no pets in the pavilion. Tone: warm, a little worn, real. No photos available. Do not invent a website, a phone number or a sponsor. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Alan Whitcomb, director of Whitcomb & Daughters Funeral Home in Bangor, Maine. Families often ask for a quiet memorial video to play during a visitation, and I want a sample to show them. I want a 60-second widescreen (16:9) video, with no voice and soft music only, that makes a grieving family feel unhurried, cared for and not sold to. It should show a life as seasons and small things: a lobster boat at dawn, a kitchen table with a coffee cup and a folded newspaper, hands tying a fishing fly, a porch light coming on at dusk, a quilt on a chair. End on a simple card: 'In loving memory' and a name line left blank for the family to fill in, then our name and 'Bangor, Maine'. The feeling to leave is peace and gratitude. The viewer should do nothing. All shots will be generated by a video model, with no recognizable faces. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Kenji Mori, owner of Mori Noodle Bar, a 14-seat ramen shop on Exchange Street in Portland, Maine. I want a 15-second vertical (9:16) reel for Instagram and TikTok to announce our winter menu, and I want people to come in this week. Facts: starts Monday, January 6; the new bowl is a miso butter corn ramen with a soft egg, $17; we also have a spicy garlic tonkotsu at $18; open Tuesday through Sunday, 5 to 10 p.m., closed Mondays after the 6th; we don't take reservations, so there is usually a line out the door when it's snowing; the broth simmers for 14 hours. Tone: cozy, a little funny, steamy. The viewer should feel hungry and want to walk in out of the cold. All shots will be generated by a video model, with no recognizable faces. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Denise Okafor, aquatics manager at Lakeside Swim Club in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. We need to hire 12 lifeguards before Memorial Day weekend, and I want a 20-second square (1:1) video for Instagram and Facebook aimed at 15 to 18 year olds and their parents. Facts: $15.50 an hour, $17 after the first summer; we pay for the certification class ($275 value) at the Sioux Falls Y on April 12 and 13; season runs May 24 to August 17; flexible schedules around summer jobs and sports; free pool pass for the whole family; apply at the front desk or through the link in our bio. Tone: bright, confident, not corny. I want teens to think 'that looks like a good job' and apply this month. All shots will be generated by a video model, with no recognizable faces. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.
